assessments.reasoning: Capture 1f1ee285fdbc419b82549c0465e3024d identifies the SPDX repository’s annotated v3.29.0 object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b. Its cited range matches and names the target as commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, exactly the revision in the W3C-20150513 detail URL. GitHub reports the tag as unsigned.

Capture abd5a1ba407e4e90b5f0b8915cc332e0 matches all five cited ranges in SPDX’s pinned detail. It gives 'W3C Software Notice and Document License (2015-05-13)', licenseId 'W3C-20150513', and isDeprecatedLicenseId false. Its references give https://www.w3.org/Consortium/Legal/2015/copyright-software-and-document, https://www.w3.org/copyright/software-license-2015/ and https://www.w3.org/copyright/software-license-2023/. Its note dates effect to May 13, 2015 and expressly permits the same ID for the January 1, 2023 changes under SPDX’s guidelines.

W3C capture 29b92083d00648d281d6957309d9183d matches the bound ranges and the 2015 URL cited by SPDX. Its heading, change to 'work', period in effect and successor link identify the exact publisher target. These details explain correspondence despite the additional word 'Notice' in the SPDX name.

Capture 9bb8b1fc4ee5468c9d413a151da8ece8 matches the cited ranges on W3C’s versioned 2023 page. W3C identifies January 1, 2023 as its effective date, links 2015 as the previous version and explicitly describes the copyright-holder identification update. This is direct publisher authority for the distinction that limits the claim. The SPDX detail supplies the separate identifier decision.

challenge.method: Compared the annotated tag target, exact SPDX name and fields, all three W3C references and their recorded link statuses, the SPDX edition note, both publisher self-links, effective dates, change statements and captured digests.
challenge.results: The 2015 URL appears explicitly alongside a legacy 2015 URL and the 2023 URL. SPDX recorded all three as non-live with match 'N/A' at its historical check. The requested 2015 and 2023 publisher acquisitions both succeeded. W3C identifies separate versions and changed copyright-holder wording, and the captures have different digests. These findings defeat an edition merge or byte-equality inference while preserving SPDX’s stated identifier reuse.

limitations: The finding concerns the selected 2015 English representation and the pinned SPDX release. It attributes the matching decision to SPDX. It establishes no exclusive one-ID-to-one-edition rule, byte equality, blanket legal equivalence, project permission or initial publication timestamp.
reasoning: SPDX 3.29.0 explicitly cites the exact 2015 publisher route under W3C-20150513. Its edition note also permits reuse of the ID for the 2023 changes under the SPDX Matching Guidelines. SCES §§1, 3, 4 and 7 require attribution to the authority for each proposition, an immutable data revision and a challenge to overbroad identity. SPDX governs its identifier treatment. W3C governs the publisher versions. Those authorities support the 2015 mapping with 2023 as material context.
